workflow.title: Moving a Windows cleanup routine to Mac: separate junk, large files and duplicates
workflow.intent: Help a former PartitionAssistant Cleanup user translate three cleanup categories into a deliberate Mac review workflow, not install a Windows utility on macOS.
workflow.description: Carry over the review habit, not Windows-specific cleanup rules. Separate rebuildable caches from large originals and suspected duplicates before choosing a Mac tool.
outline: Platform boundary first; do not confuse Cleanup with partition management or NTFS for Mac
Use the vendor's three categories as questions, not deletion permission
Review cache rebuild costs separately from irreplaceable videos, installers and backups
Duplicate detection is a separate requirement: Breathing Room parity not established
Show the first-party Space example with disclosure; official competitor review image only after permission
Bounded recommendation: Breathing Room, which we build, for documented Mac storage inspection; stay with Windows tools on Windows
workflow.distinctValue: A category-to-review decision aid: cache -> identify owner/rebuild cost; large original -> check backup/need; suspected duplicate -> establish identity/retention before any removal. No automatic deletion, benchmarks or screenshots disguised as measured output.
workflow.interactionHandoff: A non-mutating checklist asking OS, file type, backup status and rebuild cost; no filesystem access. All route availability needs checking by the drafting job.
workflow.status: blocked; brief only, no article drafted
